title: The artifact door refuses a history row without standing
intention: The artifact door refuses a history.json write that introduces a record lacking the `standing` floor projector.UNIVERSAL_REQUIRED names (a row not already present in the standing file, byte-for-byte as a parsed record), so no writer can land a new or altered history row past projector.append_entry's floor, and nothing is written when it tries.
why: Child of 471aa05ba639. Two history rows without `standing` (tester seq 64, counting_block seq 2) landed on 2026-10-02 through artifact.write with verb append from CC's python -m scripts, past projector.append_entry's floor (.artifact-journal.jsonl). The door beneath the projector does not carry the projector's floor, so the floor is policy at that entrance (Law 4).
traces_to: Law 4 (the `standing` floor is enforced at projector.append_entry but not at the artifact door beneath it; this makes it physics at the lower entrance); Law 7 (a history row is a record of truth); RULE 1 (the build lives inside cairn/tools/artifact and reads the floor only through charter's declared public interface).
how: In cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py add _refuse_history_without_floor(p, blob) beside f9ba's _refuse_non_canonical (artifact.py:356) and call it in write() right after the canonical check (artifact.py:390), when p.name == 'history.json': parse the body as a list and the standing file (if any) as a list; for each record in the body that is not equal to some record of the standing list (a new or altered row), missing = [k for k in projector.UNIVERSAL_REQUIRED if not rec.get(k)]; any missing raises Refused naming the record's seq and the missing keys, ending 'nothing written (<ticket id>)'. projector is imported at call time (`from cairn.tools.charter import projector`) because projector imports the door at module level; cairn.tools.charter.projector is charter's declared public_interface (RULE 1). The tooth is a new red-first proof in cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/ writing a scratch history.json through artifact.write with a row lacking standing (refused, file bytes unchanged) and one carrying it (written). The two live offending rows are not this child's: a whole-file history write that still carries them will be refused until the repair child lands, which is the door working. Rows already standing are not re-judged, so a pre-journal row kept as the tooth's exhibit (diagnostic_inspector seq 4) does not refuse that component's future appends, and a repair that ADDS standing to an old row passes.
falsifier: Done when a new red-first proof cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_a_history_row_without_standing_is_refused.py is green under bin/cairn test with teeth: (1) a scratch history.json write introducing a row without standing raises Refused and the file's bytes are unchanged; (2) a write introducing a row carrying standing lands; (3) a write that keeps an old standing-less row untouched and appends a row carrying standing lands (rows already standing are not re-judged). test_artifact_door.py, test_a_json_record_lands_in_one_canonical_form.py and test_append_door_instrument.py's other teeth stay green. Hollow: reverting artifact.py reds tooth 1. Horizon: PROVED this session. Wrong intent if a sanctioned writer must introduce a history row without standing.

decisions.text: There is no separate standing file. 'The standing file' is the history.json already on disk at the path being written (p itself, read before the write); its rows are the rows not re-judged. 'standing' the KEY is the field each row must carry (projector.UNIVERSAL_REQUIRED = ('standing',)). build_62a5.py already encodes this.
decisions.step: The standing file path is derivable from the history.json path (e.g., p.parent / 'standing.json', or the path is established in the codebase or parent ticket context), and standing contains a list of pre-approved history records that are not re-judged on subsequent writes.
